subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should the Telegram plugin expose a public parse/text-mode config, and which values/defaults should be supported across sends, captions, edits, and streaming previews?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix adds a public config surface whose values affect Telegram rendering, escaping, client compatibility, and security boundaries.

options.title: Add narrow plain/html config
options.body: Preserve current default behavior, add an explicit plain/no-parse mode with top-level and optionally per-account inheritance, and cover every outbound funnel before merge.

options.title: Broaden to MarkdownV2/raw/entity modes
options.body: Include MarkdownV2, raw HTML, or entity-bearing modes, accepting a larger API, escaping, and security review burden.

options.title: Keep existing knobs only
options.body: Decline a new parse-mode surface for now and continue using `richMessages`, `markdown.tables`, and targeted formatter fixes for specific Telegram rendering problems.

recommendation.title: Add narrow plain/html config
recommendation.body: Preserve current default behavior, add an explicit plain/no-parse mode with top-level and optionally per-account inheritance, and cover every outbound funnel before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest history signal for the original HTML-formatting decision and prior parse-mode product review context.
